---
title: "Extra tests"
subtitle: "Two follow-up tests: Sámi names in the thesaurus, and Annif compared with the cataloguers"
---

```{r}
source("_common.R", encoding = "UTF-8")
sami_codes <- c("sme", "smn", "sms", "sma", "smj", "sjd", "sje", "sju", "smi")
# What the main run showed for the Sámi question
sq <- "sami-handicrafts"
main_sami <- if (sq %in% qids) {
  r <- records_all[records_all$question_id == sq, ]
  stats::setNames(vapply(conds, function(c) sum(r$condition == c & r$language %in% sami_codes), numeric(1)), conds)
} else NULL
have_sami <- !is.null(sami_q) && nrow(sami_q) > 0
have_cat <- !is.null(cat_summary) && nrow(cat_summary) > 0
```

::: {.in-short}
**In short.** Two tests that go one step beyond the main study, both free to run (no AI).
**The Sámi test** asks whether Sámi-language material becomes easier to find when search C also
uses the thesaurus's Northern Sámi names: `r if (have_sami) "**results below**" else "**not run yet**"`.
**The cataloguer test** asks whether Annif would describe the records the way cataloguers did:
`r if (have_cat) "**results below**" else "**not run yet**"`.
:::

## 1. Does the thesaurus speak Sámi?

**Why this test.** The national thesaurus YSO now has Northern Sámi names for a large part of
its concepts (the National Library of Finland announced about 18,000 in February 2024). Our
search C only added Finnish, Swedish and English names. `r if (!is.null(main_sami) && main_sami[["C_finto"]] < main_sami[["A_direct"]]) sprintf("In the main run, the *Sámi handicrafts* question kept **%s** Sámi-language records in search A but only **%s** in search C: the Finnish and Swedish names pulled other records into the top 60, and nothing pulled Sámi records back.", main_sami[["A_direct"]], main_sami[["C_finto"]]) else if (!is.null(main_sami)) sprintf("In the main run, the *Sámi handicrafts* question kept %s Sámi-language records in search A and %s in search C.", main_sami[["A_direct"]], main_sami[["C_finto"]]) else ""`
So a standard that speaks the national languages, but not Sámi, may push Sámi material out of
view. That is a question about **power**, and the abstract promises to look at it.

**What the test does.** It runs every question **twice, at the same time**: search C with
Finnish, Swedish and English names (as before), and search C with Northern Sámi names added.
Nothing else changes, and the test checks that searches A and B came out the same both times.

```{r}
#| results: asis
if (!have_sami) {
  cat("::: {.callout-note}\n## Not run yet\n\nRun this from the heritageRAG folder (free, takes a few minutes):\n\n",
      "```bash\nRscript scripts/run_sami_sensitivity.R inst/extdata/study_questions.csv results/sami-sensitivity\n```\n\n",
      "Then copy the results into this report and render it again:\n\n",
      "```bash\nRscript prepare_data.R ../heritageRAG/results/final ../heritageRAG/results/batch-pilot ../heritageRAG/results/sami-sensitivity\nquarto render\n```\n\n",
      "This section then shows, for every question, which Sámi words were added, how much bigger search C became, ",
      "and how many Sámi-language records it kept with and without the Sámi words.\n:::\n", sep = "")
}
```

```{r}
#| results: asis
if (have_sami) {
  s <- sami_summary
  run_date <- if (!is.null(sami_run)) format(as.Date(substr(sami_run$run_date[1], 1, 10)), "%d %B %Y") else "-"
  cat(sprintf("The test ran on %s with %s questions. Finto returned a Northern Sámi name for **%s of %s** thesaurus concepts used in search C, and the Sámi names added new search words in **%s** questions.\n\n",
              run_date, s$questions, s$concepts_with_extra_label, s$concepts, s$questions_with_added_terms))
  cat(sprintf("Across all questions, search C kept **%s Sámi-language records without the Sámi names and %s with them**. The number went up in %s question%s and down in %s.\n\n",
              s$focus_records_base, s$focus_records_alt, s$questions_focus_up, ifelse(s$questions_focus_up == 1, "", "s"),
              s$questions_focus_down))
  if (s$concepts_with_extra_label == 0) {
    callout("warning", "No Sámi names came back",
            "Finto returned no Northern Sámi names, so both runs used the same words. Check the finto package's label request for the language code `se` before reading anything into this test.")
  }
  if (s$questions_other_conditions_changed > 0) {
    callout("warning", "Searches A or B changed between the two runs",
            sprintf("In %s question(s) searches A or B were not the same in both runs (Annif or Finto answered differently). Compare search C only where A and B stayed the same.", s$questions_other_conditions_changed))
  }
  q <- sami_q[match(intersect(qids, sami_q$question_id), sami_q$question_id), ]
  if (!nrow(q)) q <- sami_q
  t <- data.frame(
    Question = qname(q$question_id),
    `Sámi words added` = q$terms_added,
    `Matching in Finna (without → with)` = paste(num(q$index_matches_base), "→", num(q$index_matches_alt)),
    `Sámi-language records kept (without → with)` = paste(q$focus_records_base, "→", q$focus_records_alt),
    `Records in common` = pct(q$jaccard),
    check.names = FALSE)
  cat(paste(knitr::kable(t, row.names = FALSE), collapse = "\n"), "\n\n")
  cat("<p class=\"how-to-read\">How to read this: \"without\" is search C with Finnish, Swedish and English names; \"with\" adds the Northern Sámi names. Sámi-language records are those Finna labels as a Sámi language (North, Inari, Skolt and other Sámi, or Sámi in general). Records in common: the share of records the two versions of search C share. When the number of matches stays the same but the records change, the Sámi words matched no new records but changed Finna's ranking, which gives more weight to records that contain more of the search words.</p>\n\n")
}
```

```{r}
#| fig-height: 4.2
#| fig-alt: "Paired bars per question: Sámi-language records kept by search C without and with Northern Sámi names."
if (have_sami) {
  q <- sami_q[sami_q$focus_records_base > 0 | sami_q$focus_records_alt > 0, ]
  if (nrow(q)) {
    q <- q[order(q$focus_records_alt), ]
    chart_par(mar = c(4, 15, 2.6, 1.5))
    m <- rbind(q$focus_records_base, q$focus_records_alt)
    bp <- graphics::barplot(m, beside = TRUE, horiz = TRUE, names.arg = qname(q$question_id),
                            col = c("#CDBBD7", cond_col[["C_finto"]]), border = NA, cex.names = 0.85,
                            xlab = "Sámi-language records among the 60 kept", xlim = c(0, max(m, 1) * 1.15))
    graphics::text(m, bp, m, pos = 4, cex = 0.75, col = "#55636B")
    graphics::legend("top", inset = c(0, -0.12), xpd = TRUE, horiz = TRUE, bty = "n", fill = c("#CDBBD7", cond_col[["C_finto"]]),
                     border = NA, legend = c("C without Sámi names", "C with Sámi names"), cex = 0.85)
  }
}
```

```{r}
#| results: asis
if (have_sami) {
  q <- sami_q[sami_q$focus_records_base > 0 | sami_q$focus_records_alt > 0, ]
  if (!nrow(q)) cat("No question kept any Sámi-language records in either version of search C.\n\n")
  if (!is.null(sami_terms) && nrow(sami_terms)) {
    cat("**The Sámi words that were added**\n\n")
    tt <- stats::aggregate(term ~ question_id + anchor, data = sami_terms, FUN = function(x) paste0("*", unique(x), "*", collapse = ", "))
    tt <- tt[order(match(tt$question_id, qids)), ]
    cat(paste(knitr::kable(data.frame(Question = qname(tt$question_id), `Key word` = tt$anchor,
                                      `Northern Sámi names added` = tt$term, check.names = FALSE), row.names = FALSE), collapse = "\n"), "\n\n")
  }
  via <- sum(sami_q$focus_records_via_extra)
  cat(sprintf("**What it means.** %s\n\n",
    if (sami_summary$focus_records_alt > sami_summary$focus_records_base) {
      paste0(sprintf("When the standard includes Sámi names, search C keeps more Sámi-language material (%s against %s records). %s of the Sámi-language records in the new version match through one of the added Sámi words. ",
              sami_summary$focus_records_alt, sami_summary$focus_records_base, via),
             if (!is.null(main_sami) && sq %in% sami_q$question_id) {
               z <- sami_q[sami_q$question_id == sq, ]
               sprintf("For the *Sámi handicrafts* question the order is telling: our own words (search A) kept %s Sámi-language records, the Finnish, Swedish and English thesaurus terms cut that to %s, and adding the Sámi names raised it to %s. ",
                       main_sami[["A_direct"]], z$focus_records_base, z$focus_records_alt)
             } else "",
             "Which material a researcher sees depends on which languages the vocabulary standard speaks.")
    } else if (sami_summary$focus_records_alt == sami_summary$focus_records_base) {
      "Adding Sámi names did not change how many Sámi-language records search C kept. Either few Sámi records exist for these topics, or the catalogues describe them with Finnish and Swedish words anyway."
    } else {
      "Adding Sámi names left fewer Sámi-language records in search C. Check the added words: a Sámi word that also matches many other records can push Sámi records out of the top 60."
    }))
  cat("**Be careful.** Many records give no language, so these counts are a floor. Most questions are not about Sámi topics, so the test mainly matters for the Sámi question and a few others. The Sámi words come from YSO as published in Finto on the test date.\n\n")
}
```

## 2. Would Annif describe the records the way cataloguers did?

**Why this test.** Annif is used to suggest subject words for new catalogue records. In the
main study we only used it on the *question*. This test turns it around: Annif reads the title
and description of each record the AI saw (never its subject words) and suggests subject words,
which are then compared with the words the cataloguers chose. Words are compared through their
YSO names in Finnish, Swedish and English, so *naiset* and *women* count as the same word.

```{r}
#| results: asis
if (!have_cat) {
  cat("::: {.callout-note}\n## Not run yet\n\nRun this from the heritageRAG folder (free; it only reads from Annif):\n\n",
      "```bash\nRscript scripts/annif_vs_catalogue.R results/final\n```\n\n",
      "Then run prepare_data.R and quarto render again. This section then shows how many of the cataloguers' subject words Annif also suggests, ",
      "and examples of words only one of them used.\n:::\n", sep = "")
} else {
  s <- cat_summary
  cat(sprintf("Annif indexed **%s** records; %s of them have no subject words in the catalogue. For the **%s** records that have both, Annif suggested on average **%s** of the cataloguers' subject words, and at least one shared word for **%s** of the records.\n\n",
              s$indexed, s$without_catalogue_subjects, s$records_scored, pct(s$mean_catalogue_recall), pct(s$any_shared_share)))
  if (!is.null(cat_by) && nrow(cat_by)) {
    b <- cat_by[match(conds, cat_by$condition), ]
    cat(paste(knitr::kable(data.frame(`Records found by` = cond_short, Records = b$records,
                                      `Cataloguers' words Annif also suggested` = pct(b$mean_catalogue_recall),
                                      `Records with at least one shared word` = pct(b$any_shared_share), check.names = FALSE),
                           row.names = FALSE), collapse = "\n"), "\n\n")
    cat("<p class=\"how-to-read\">A record found by several searches counts in each of their rows.</p>\n\n")
  }
  ex <- cat_records[!is.na(cat_records$catalogue_recall) & nzchar(cat_records$catalogue_only) & nzchar(cat_records$annif_only), ]
  ex <- utils::head(ex[order(-ex$catalogue_subjects), ], 5)
  if (nrow(ex)) {
    cat("**Examples: words only one side used**\n\n")
    cut <- function(x) ifelse(nchar(x) > 90, paste0(substr(x, 1, 89), "..."), x)
    cat(paste(knitr::kable(data.frame(Question = qname(ex$question_id), `Both` = ifelse(nzchar(ex$shared_subjects), cut(ex$shared_subjects), "-"),
                                      `Only the cataloguers` = cut(ex$catalogue_only), `Only Annif` = cut(ex$annif_only),
                                      check.names = FALSE), row.names = FALSE), collapse = "\n"), "\n\n")
  }
  cat("**What it means.** The gap between the two lists shows how differently an automatic indexer and a person describe the same record. Where catalogues rely more on automatic indexing, the words that make records findable shift in the same way.\n\n")
  cat("**Be careful.** This is exploratory. Catalogue subject words come without thesaurus links, so they are matched by name; a word written differently counts as different. Annif only sees the short title and description that Finna returns.\n\n")
}
```

Sources: [National Library of Finland: YSO now also in Northern Sámi](https://www.kansalliskirjasto.fi/en/news/general-finnish-ontology-yso-now-also-available-northern-sami);
[IFLA: support for North Sámi at the National Library of Finland](https://www.ifla.org/news/introducing-support-for-the-indigenous-north-sami-language-at-the-national-library-of-finland/).
